title: perf_event_open ring buffer page (perf_event_mmap_page)
summary: The perf_event_open(2) syscall returns a file descriptor; mmap'ing it gives a shared memory region whose first page is a perf_event_mmap_page control structure. It contains the data_head/data_tail pointers (for the ring buffer), time conversion parameters (for converting hardware timestamps to nanoseconds), and capability bits.

ext.summary: The perf_event_open(2) syscall returns a file descriptor; mmap'ing it gives a shared memory region whose first page is a perf_event_mmap_page control structure. It contains the data_head/data_tail pointers (for the ring buffer), time conversion parameters (for converting hardware timestamps to nanoseconds), and capability bits.

structure.meaning: Seqlock for consistent reads of the time fields.
Offset to add to the raw counter value.
Time the event was enabled (in nanoseconds).
Time the event was running (accounts for multiplexing).
Capability bits: cap_usr_time, cap_usr_rdpmc, cap_bit0_is_deprecated, etc.
Width of the PMU counter in bits.
Shift for time conversion: (time_enabled - time_zero) >> time_shift.
Head of the data ring (written by kernel; read by userspace).
Tail of the data ring (written by userspace; read by kernel).
Offset from mmap base to the data ring.
Size of the data ring (power of 2).

notes: The ring buffer stores perf_event_header records (type, size, plus type-specific data: sample, mmap, comm, fork, exit, ...).
time_enabled/time_running account for multiplexing when more events than PMU counters.
rdpmc (cap_usr_rdpmc) allows userspace to read the PMU counter directly without a syscall.
perf_event_open can profile hardware counters, software events, tracepoints, kprobes, uprobes, and BPF programs.
